results.reason: Issue 1 identifies MSA § 3.2 as nationwide exclusivity for all warehousing, freight and delivery, contrasts it with Term Sheet § 4.1 (last-mile home delivery, NYC metro only), and gives replacement language tracking the term sheet.

Issue 2 explains that § 11.3 carves Customer's § 10.2 indemnity out of the cap while Provider's § 10.1 stays under the 12-month cap, describes the one-sided unlimited exposure, and recommends deleting the carve-out or making it mutual.

Issue 3 identifies DPA § 9.1's Delaware law and Wilmington courts, notes the conflict with MSA § 18.1, states the DPA prevails under § 2.3, and recommends conforming the DPA to the MSA's New York choice.
Issue 4 identifies the 3-year auto-renewal with a 15-day notice window, explains the lock-in risk, and proposes 1-year renewals with a 90-day notice right.
The memo never mentions SOW § 8.2 or the one-sided assignment issue under MSA § 17.4.
It states that § 2.3 ranks the DPA first, then the MSA, then the SOW.
It states the cap is 'the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.'
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner, and each issue gives Where, What it says / Why it matters, and Recommended fix.
The issues are expressly ordered by importance, and Part IV lists items to raise with the client before the next draft.
The memo concludes the DPA's Delaware clause controls data disputes and that the documents conflict.
The memo states the exclusivity clause is far broader than the term sheet scope.
